highlights.title: Adobe Premiere finally brings powerful video editing to Android, and it's free
highlights.summary: Video editing has never been Android's strong suit. While Apple has long offered iMovie for iPhone and iPad, Google has never had a comparable offering. Adobe is now stepping up to fill this feature gap with a proper version of Premiere.
body: Android's version of Premiere doesn't offer all the features you'd get in the desktop application, but it's a big step up from the soon-to-be-retired Premiere Rush app. You can import as many video tracks as you want, trim them, split them, add effects, and export videos in up to 4K resolution. It can even extract audio from clips, reduce background noise, and add voiceovers. The app emphasizes the YouTube Short format, even defaulting your video outputs to portrait 16:9, but you can change that to something more traditional.

On a standard smartphone, the app splits the screen with the timeline at the bottom and preview up top. Adobe says that Premiere is optimized for multiple form factors. If you've got a foldable phone, the UI adjusts to give you more breathing room, placing the timeline to the right of the video. That makes sense as the default, as Premiere really wants you to make YouTube Shorts, but if you're working with something wider, there's a layout toggle that puts the widescreen video above the expanded timeline. The split is also adjustable if you want to make your video or timeline larger.
points: Video editing has never been Android's strong suit.

highlights.title: Poitras Center to fuel early careers of 50 young scientists dedicated to psychiatric disorders research
highlights.summary: Patricia and James Poitras ’63 provide fellowships for graduate students and postdocs who will shape the future of mental health research.
body: Patricia and James Poitras ’63, longtime MIT supporters, have launched a fellowship program for graduate students and postdocs studying major mental illness, expanding their MIT philanthropy to directly support early-career scientists. The commitment establishes 50 two-year fellowships through the Poitras Center for Psychiatric Disorders Research at MIT’s McGovern Institute for Brain Research. Five fellowships will be awarded every year for the next decade, creating a long-term talent pipeline focused specifically on psychiatric disorders.

The $10 million gift is the latest in a series of philanthropic investments from the Poitras family to strengthen MIT’s capacity to address the growing burden of severe depression and anxiety, bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, and other complex psychiatric conditions. “Pat and Jim have remained steadfast in their decades-long commitment to bold research that can transform mental wellness,” says Robert Desimone, director of the McGovern Institute and head of the Poitras Center. “Their remarkable support of rising talent in the MIT ecosystem is yet another emblem of their commitment to that cause.”

highlights.summary: There seems to be an endless supply of untold Lord of the Rings tales for fans to explore. Even though The Fellowship of the Ring was first published in 1954 — with The Hobbit arriving even earlier in 1937 — we're still finding new ways to dig into Middle-earth lore.
body: This summer alone has brought a surprise re-release of The Lord of the Rings: War in the North, a first look at The Hunt for Gollum, and new details about the upcoming third season of The Rings of Power. Now, fans have another reason to return to Middle-earth: The One Ring tabletop RPG is getting a major update, and its crowdfunding campaign is already smashing its goals.

Free League Publishing launched its latest crowdfunding campaign for The One Ring on Hobbit Day, the fictional birthday shared by Bilbo and Frodo Baggins. The campaign set a relatively modest funding goal of $50,000, but it blew past that figure in less than an hour.
And it hasn't slowed down since. The campaign has now raised more than $1.1 million from nearly 5,000 backers, more than 22 times its original goal, with 23 days still remaining.

highlights.title: Introducing GPT-6 Sol and Luna
highlights.summary: Meet GPT-6 Sol and Luna, two models that bring frontier intelligence to everyday work with different balances of capability and cost.
body: More ways to bring frontier intelligence into the work you do every day.

Earlier this month, we introduced GPT‑6 Astra, the most intelligent and aligned model in the world. While the most demanding and important projects still call for Astra’s full depth, work happens at different scales, rhythms, and budgets.

That’s why we’re expanding the GPT‑6 universe with GPT‑6 Sol and GPT‑6 Luna. GPT‑6 Astra introduced a new generation of intelligence—these models help distribute the benefits of that intelligence by advancing the frontier on cost efficiency. We trained GPT‑6 Sol and Luna with similar methods as GPT‑6 Astra, bringing the advances behind Astra’s state-of-the-art performance in professional work, factuality, coding, computer use, and alignment to faster, more affordable models.

highlights.title: Jacks stars as England beat Sri Lanka in first ODI
highlights.summary: England continued their white-ball dominance over Sri Lanka as an 89-run victory in the first ODI in Durham saw them take a 1-0 lead in the three-match series.
body: Will Jacks starred with bat and ball, hitting an handy 46 not out off 47 balls before completing a career-best 5-22 to wrap up the Sri Lankan tail.
Captain Harry Brook (67 off 69 balls) top-scored after electing to bat at the toss but a middle order wobble inspired by debutant Sachindu Colombage (3-44) restricted England to 265 in 48.1 overs.
England took steady wickets to hamper Sri Lanka's pursuit of 266 before Jacks struck three times in the final over as the tourists were bowled out for 176 in 37 overs.
England's decision to bat first after winning the toss was immediately tested when Tom Banton fell to a jaffa from Asitha Fernando, the delivery nipping back to clip the bail on top of off stump.

highlights.title: Xbox is Turning its Back on Xbox Game Studios
highlights.summary: But there's more going on here than just a new home for Halo. On Tuesday, Microsoft announced a confusion of other moves in the name of "operating fewer business units, aligning groups that already work closely together, and focusing our publishing expertise."
body: The most eye-catching thing about Xbox's latest layoffs and the consolidation of its studios is the dramatic change coming to Halo. The game series that started it all for Xbox is being rebooted under Activision, and Halo Studios is being gutted — all but closed, really. Sixteen years after Bungie left for good, the attempt to build a non-Bungie studio to make Halo games begins anew. Second time lucky, I guess.

Rare and World's Edge (which collaborates with outside studios on the Age of Empires strategy games) go to Activision. Obsidian Entertainment goes to Bethesda — I assume not to be swallowed into the developer Bethesda Game Studios, but to join the family of studios under the banner of publisher Bethesda Softworks, alongside the likes of MachineGames and Id Software. Microsoft Casual Games goes to Candy Crush maker King, which used to be part of Activision but is now its own unit. Playground Games and Turn 10 are being merged.

These moves might appear unrelated, but they have a common theme. Or rather, a common direction of travel. You'll notice that, with the exception of Playground and Turn 10's merger, they all involve developers leaving the Xbox Game Studios group.

highlights.title: Andreessen Horowitz is launching an ‘academy’ with no homework and partnerships with Palantir, Google, and Meta
highlights.summary: Venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) is creating an "academy" positioned as a pipeline for young people to build or join a Silicon Valley startup. The "Horowitz Andreessen Academy" will launch with 10 partners, including Anduril, Anthropic, Coinbase, Google, Meta, NVIDIA, OpenAI…
body: The Horowitz Andreessen Academy trades degrees and homework for stints at tech companies.

To partake in the one-year program, students will have to move to San Francisco and arrange their own housing, according to the academy’s FAQ page. Students are promised more than $50,000 in compute credits and a $5,000 travel and research budget offered by a16z. The announcement says they’ll have “no traditional grades, tests, or homework,” but will “learn from Silicon Valley’s most storied founders and operators in short, high-impact classes and spend the rest of your time working and exploring.”

The academy seems like the latest attempt by Silicon Valley’s billionaires to “fix” America’s education system by creating their own. Elon Musk, Mark Zuckerberg, and Jeff Bezos have all poured money into starting their own schools, while a16z founders Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz have been critical of colleges. Last year, Andreessen reportedly called Stanford and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology “political lobbying operations fighting American innovation” in a group chat with White House officials and tech leaders, according to The Washington Post.

highlights.title: Skirts given star billing as Prada swerves trousers and dresses in Milan
highlights.summary: Combination of Miuccia Prada with Belgian designer Raf Simons once again spins gold for fashion house. Miuccia Prada’s style formula is simple: begin with a great skirt. Her personal uniform is a knee-length skirt, A-line or pleated, most often with a plain sweater and kitten heels.
body: The Prada collection that opened Milan fashion week made a compelling case for her favourite outfit, with a skirt the star of every one of the 63 looks – no dresses, no trousers. It won the room over, so expect to see the personality skirt on a high street near you soon.

For the past six years, Miuccia Prada has shared design duties with Belgian designer Raf Simons, 20 years her junior. The arrangement was considered unusual when announced, but the house of Prada has always had a way of spinning gold from quirky ideas, and it has worked.
“She had the idea to focus on skirts this time,” Simons explained before this show. “And I said, why not make it an all-skirt show?”

She prefers skirts to dresses because “they give you room for contrast”, Mrs Prada said. “The way I think and feel is complicated, contradictory. If I wear something feminine, I want to wear something masculine too. A dress is all one idea, and we are never just one idea.”

highlights.title: How to Claim Your Cut of Apple’s $250 Million Siri Settlement
highlights.summary: Apple may pay out up to $95 for each eligible iPhone purchased by someone who felt misled about Siri’s release. You have until December 21 to submit a claim.
body: In May, Apple agreed to pay out $250 million as part of a class action lawsuit over claims the company overhyped its Apple Intelligence tools, specifically the long-delayed Siri AI overhaul.

Although the revamped Siri AI voice assistant is now available for owners of newer iPhones via iOS 27, you may still be eligible to claim cash back for past purchases. This settlement covers customers in the US who made their purchases from June 10, 2024 to March 29, 2025, and bought certain iPhone 15 or iPhone 16 models from Apple. If you qualify, you might receive up to $95 for each phone.

This settlement revolves around Apple’s promotion of Siri features to sell iPhones. “I expected to receive a Siri Apple Intelligence feature and did not receive it,” reads part of the statement you have to sign when filling out the claim form. As part of the settlement, Apple denies any wrongdoing.
“We resolved this matter to stay focused on doing what we do best, delivering the most innovative products and services to our users,” read part of Apple’s statement from May about the settlement.
points: Apple may pay out up to $95 for each eligible iPhone purchased by someone who felt misled about Siri’s release.

highlights.title: Rabbit Is Back, This Time With an AI Agent App
highlights.summary: Two years after trying to sidestep mobile apps with dedicated AI hardware, Rabbit is launching OS3, a cross-platform agent that lives on the screens you already use.
body: Lyu's gadget was among the first in the gold rush to create dedicated AI hardware that acted as a virtual assistant. You could speak into the R1 and ask it to complete tasks for you—book an Uber; order food on DoorDash. After a buzzy launch at CES 2024, it earned scathing reviews. All the agentic stuff on the R1 just didn't work that well. WIRED gave it a 3/10.
Since those early days, the capabilities of AI assistants have vastly improved, and now the tech is all the rage. So Rabbit is banging the drum again.

On Tuesday, Rabbit announced OS3, a standalone “agentic operating system” designed to run across multiple screens. It also arrives as a software update for the company's R1 gadget, though you don't need an R1 to use it. Instead, you can access OS3 through a desktop browser, Telegram on your phone, or even iMessage.
It’s a striking pivot for a company that once championed the handheld hardware over smartphone apps, but the environment for this type of software has ripened.
points: Two years after trying to sidestep mobile apps with dedicated AI hardware, Rabbit is launching OS3, a cross-platform agent that lives on the screens you already use.

highlights.title: WoW: Forever Aspires To Have A “Mandela Effect” On Players
highlights.summary: World of Warcraft: Forever is reinventing the classic version of Azeroth with all kinds of new content, and if Blizzard does its job, players won't be able to tell the difference between what's old and what's new.
body: Announced during BlizzCon 2026, Forever introduces four new zones to Azeroth: the Riverglades, Mount Hjyal, Shen'dralas, and Zephras Isle. In an interview with GameSpot, WoW: Forever senior art director Jeff Parrott and senior game designer Josh Greenfield elaborated on how Blizzard approached developing these all-new zones so that they don't feel out of place in a 22-year old game, as well as how they tried to capture how players "remember" Azeroth looking.
Parrott said the team spent a lot of time looking back at the original, "vanilla" version of WoW and trying to understand how zones were designed back in 2004 when the game first released.

"The team did a great job of just digging in there," Parrott said. "Riverglades is a great example. I think that's a full new zone that we have, and really did a great job of leaning into that Vanilla-era kind of ethos for the design, the flow in the way everything kind of moves through the zone, the quests move you through the zone. It does feel extremely of that era, of that time. So it's really just understanding what we're aiming for and staying faithful to it."
He said the goal was for Forever's new zones to feel "familiar, but new."

highlights.title: Why you should quit and not look back: ‘Saying yes to everything is saying no to what matters’
highlights.summary: In her new book, The Case For Quitting: The Surprising Benefits of Opting Out, Lindsay Crouse discusses the costs and traps of never giving up – and how she set herself free. Lindsay Crouse used to define herself as not a quitter.
body: She went to Harvard University, where she learned to become even more high-achieving and ambitious, then landed an assistant job at the New York Times and worked her way up to become an opinion writer and producer. On the weekends, Crouse ran marathons and did endurance sports, clocking new personal bests throughout her thirties.
“My entire life was really guided by only one question: how can I go harder, and do more?” she says now over Zoom.

Over time, though, that mentality began to backfire. After having two children, Crouse started falling behind, dropping balls and losing her passion for running and writing. Something needed to change.

Now Crouse argues quitting is essential for a satisfying, successful life. She herself left her prestigious job to chase unknown risks and rewards. “We need to start viewing quitting as a tool of perseverance, rather than the enemy of it,” she said. “If we find ourselves in a hole, often we dig harder when we should just stop digging.”

The standout performances, however, come from Ajeigbe and Ba, who make for believable lovers and coerced conspirators, always weighing their love for each other and ambition for success against the circumstances they find themselves in. It’s hard to look elsewhere when he’s in the frame.

highlights.title: AI Models Built From Rat Brains Just Got Closer to Reality
highlights.summary: The Biological Computing Company is bringing its AI tools to Amazon Web Services in a major boost for a once-fringe field that aims to marry nature with code.
body: A biological computing startup that uses neural patterns from rat brain cells to build artificial intelligence just got a major boost from Amazon.

Starting Tuesday, select Amazon Web Services customers will gain access to The Biological Computing Company’s “rat brain” AI model as part of a limited preview. The startup’s technology is specifically designed to improve AI for generating videos. Both Amazon and The Biological Computing Company, which goes by the acronym TBC, says they expect the tech to roll out to all AWS enterprise customers soon.

“We figured out a way to code information, like images for example, to the biological material,” says TBC cofounder Alexander Ksendzovsky. “We then observe how the biology processes that information, and then we build a tool that mimics that process.”
